title: Fixed-beta Gibbs-weighted cancellation for the resolvent force term
question: Can the V'(q)f'(q) second-commutator term be paired by a fixed-beta one-site Gibbs integration-by-parts identity, replacing the divergent standalone K-form multiplier by f'' and the derivative-bearing history?
method: Use the exact Q3 one-site potential V=17/12-q^2/2+3q^4/20 and the resolvent coordinate f(q)=16q/(16+q^2). Verify the completed-square form V=1+(3/20)(q^2-5/3)^2 and the global quartic tail V>=q^4/20 on an exact rational two-sided grid.

Verify the quotient-rule formulas for f' and f'', their exact finite-grid envelopes |f'|<=1 and |f''|<=1, and the product-rule expression (f'h)'=f''h+f'h' for derivative-bearing polynomial history proxies.

Use the compact-support fixed-beta Gibbs integration-by-parts contract omega_beta(V'f'h)=beta^(-1)omega_beta((f'h)') and apply Cauchy-Schwarz to obtain the conditional matrix-element envelope beta^(-1)(||h||_2+||h'||_2). The explicit beta dependence is retained.
Reproduce all rational rows in a separate Fraction-only implementation and compile Lean R309 for the potential completion, quartic tail, derivative formulas and beta envelope coefficient.
finding: Primary 135/135, independent 77/77, integrated 12/12, and Lean R309 PASS. The fixed-beta one-site Gibbs pairing transfers the force factor from V'f'h to the derivative-bearing product f''h+f'h' under the declared compact-support zero-boundary contract. Because |f'| and |f''| are bounded by one on the audited grid, the resulting conditional matrix-element envelope is beta^(-1)(||h||_2+||h'||_2), with no standalone V'f' multiplier. This is a finite state-weighted cancellation bridge, not a squared V-weighted K-form estimate.
